newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei clambers above 20,000 line by close.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei clambers above 20,000 line by close.

text.p: Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei 225 index climbed back above 20,000 threshold on Monday as investors, including pension funds, actively sought high-technology issues backed by firm earnings, brokers said.

They said a media report of optimistic comments on Tokyo stocks by a top policy-maker of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) late in the afternoon also helped buoy the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares.
The Nikkei ended up 353.23 points or 1.78 percent at 20,228.72.
Its September futures added 400 points to close at 20,240.

"Pensions were out shopping today for high-techs and so were some foreign investors," said Tokyo Securities general manager Kunihiro Hatae. "The buying successfully overpowered the profit-taking moves, which were strong above 20,000."
Semiconductor-related issues rose. Advantest Corp, a semiconductor equipment maker, jumped to a new high for calendar 1997 before retracing slightly to end at 9,800 yen, up 150.
Sony Corp, which has led the market higher in past months, matched its lifetime high of 10,100 with a leap of 230 yen.

"Domestic institutions trading on behalf of pension funds have started trickling into the market again," a broker at a middle-sized brokerage said. "Such money has a habit of flowing to firms backed by solid earnings."
Late in the session, Jiji news agency reported LDP top policy-maker Taku Yamasaki as saying the Nikkei average will likely rise above 21,000 by the end of this summer, boosting the market further.
"The comment pushed futures out of the range where they had been stuck, taking cash stocks along with them," a trader at a middle-sized brokerage said.
An LDP official said she was unable to immediately confirm the report.

Shares of supermarket chain operator Yaohan Japan Corp and contractors Tada Corp and Aoki Corp topped the list of percentage gainers on the first section of the Tokyo bourse due to technical short-covering.
The three firms' shares fell sharply last week amid concerns over their financial health, traders said.
Yaohan ended up by its daily limit after adding 30 yen or 31.58 percent to reach 125 yen. It was followed by Tada, which added 26 yen or 22.61 percent to end at 141.
Aoki climbed 14 yen to 98. "People were keen to buy them back for now to see what will happen to the companies," said Katsumichi Shimizu, general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co.
With the Nikkei average ending above the 20,000 barrier, market sources said the index should gradually start consolidating near that level.

"Falls beneath 20,000 would probably be short-term corrections," said Masanobu Kaizu, a strategist at Nomura Securities Financial Research Centre. But he and other strategists said the double-tiered state of the market was likely to continue.
"The focus will be on individual issues," said Toyo Securities strategist Haruo Nakaharu.

"Shares like Advantest and Sony in the high-tech sector and Nippon Television Network Corp in the information and broadcasting sectors should see active trade, while construction sector shares and other domestic demand-oriented issues struggle."
Turnover was 420 million, compared with 427 million on Friday. Winners beat losers 607 to 469, with 157 unchanged.
The TOPIX index was up 20.75 points or 1.38 percent at 1,525.14.
The Nikkei 300 rose 4.88 points or 1.67 percent to 296.43.
The second-section index slipped 0.37 point or 0.02 percent to 1,818.68. In late afternoon the over-the-counter index was up 1.01 points or 0.09 percent at 1,187.24.
By sector, precision instruments, banks, rubber, shipbuilding and securities shares topped the list of gainers. Gas and electric power were the main retreaters.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
